themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints surged to 8 complaints THIS WEEK versus a baseline average of 0.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,100% spike (z-score: 17.9)—suggesting a coordinated posting campaign or enforcement gap in CD 314.
evidence: 8 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3,100% increase)
Z-score of 17.9 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Spike concentrated in single week suggests acute event rather than gradual trend
reporting_angles: Map the locations of illegal postings to identify if they target a specific corridor (e.g., near subway, commercial strip, political/real estate interest)
Interview Sanitation and Parks enforcement to determine if staffing or equipment changes triggered the spike, or if a particular entity is behind the campaign

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge in Midwood
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 21 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 2.5 per week—a 740% spike (z-score: 10.26)—indicating either a new crew activity or a sudden lapse in city removal.
evidence: 21 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (740% increase)
Z-score of 10.26 indicates high statistical significance
Spike mirrors illegal posting surge, suggesting concurrent quality-of-life degradation
reporting_angles: Photograph and geo-map graffiti locations to determine if tags are from one crew or multiple; check for gang markers or political messaging
Interview Parks Dept. about removal backlogs and whether budget or staffing constraints are delaying cleanups

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints exploded to 86 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 22 per week—a 291% spike (z-score: 4.72)—coinciding with construction permitting surge and rezoning activity.
evidence: 86 street/sidewalk noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 22 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (291% increase)
313 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (230 alterations + 34 new buildings) suggest active construction across district
Coincides with 187% spike in construction/plumbing complaints (47 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 16.4 avg)
reporting_angles: Cross-reference noise complaints with DOB permit locations to map construction hotspots and identify patterns (e.g., time-of-day violations, complaint concentration)
Interview residents in high-complaint blocks about construction schedules and whether early-morning or late-night work is violating noise codes

themes_detail.label: Construction & Plumbing Boom
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints spiked to 47 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 16.4 per week—a 187% increase (z-score: 6.32)—aligned with 313 DOB permits and 5 active rezoning projects.
evidence: 47 construction/plumbing complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 16.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (187% spike)
Z-score of 6.32 indicates high statistical significance
313 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (230 alterations, 34 new buildings, 10 full demolitions)
5 active ULURP/rezoning applications in pipeline (Coney Island Ave., Nostrand Ave., Flatbush Ave., plus 2 historic district reviews)
reporting_angles: Investigate whether rezoning applications are triggering speculative demolitions or rapid-fire alterations; cross-check permit locations against ULURP sites
Interview Community Board 314 and local elected officials about whether construction impact reviews are sufficient, or if noise/traffic protocols are being violated

themes_detail.label: Rodent Complaints Rising
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints nearly doubled to 25 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 12.6 per week—a 98% increase (z-score: 4.77)—reflecting potential sanitation gaps during construction season.
evidence: 25 rodent complaints LAST WEEK vs. 12.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (98% increase)
Coincides with construction activity surge; open demolitions and altered buildings may be displacing rodent populations
However, unsanitary condition complaints DOWN 45% THIS WEEK (43 vs. 78.6 avg), suggesting possible displacement effect rather than new infestations
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Health Dept. and Sanitation about whether construction-driven rodent displacement is documented; ask if bait programs are being deployed at demolition/alteration sites
Profile a block with elevated rodent complaints to understand whether residents perceive construction as the trigger
